can_do_statement: Can use 'anything' after a negative verb form.
example_raw:
You don't have to bring anything. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Italian; Pass)

When I want to eat something in the night, I can't find anything because it is too dark. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'anything' instead of 'something' after negative verbs.

positives: I don't have anything to wear.
She hasn't seen anything.

example_raw:
Have you got something else to do on Saturday or can you come with me? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Italian; Pass)

We have to bring some paints, but nothing else. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Spanish - European; Pass)

If you need anything else, you'll find it in the classroom. (Lebanon; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Arabic - Levant; Pass)

I'm going to a rock concert on Saturday, but I have three tickets for two people (me and my brother) and I am looking for someone else to go with me, so, would you like to go? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

positives: Do you need anything else?
I have someone else in mind.

can_do_statement: Can modify 'something' or 'anything' with 'to' infinitive, to make it more specific.
example_raw:
Please, bring something to drink. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Italian; Pass)

Bring some sweets and something to wear if you get cold. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; French; Pass)

I had to buy them because I didn't have anything to wear on my holidays. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Specifying purpose for an indefinite entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Adding an infinitive verb to explain what the 'something' or 'anything' is for.

positives: I need something to drink.
Do you have anything to say?
negatives: She sent anything to the wrong address.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of indefinite pronouns as objects or complements.
example_raw:
I often watch TV, because my computer is broken and I have nothing to do. (Georgia (Republic of); B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Georgian; Pass)

… there was nothing on the wall. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Gujarati; Pass)

It's a tennis club and the people there were all strangers for me, I didn't know anyone. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

When I arrived at his house there wasn't anyone there. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

He went everywhere in the world! (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Indefinite entities acting as recipients or descriptors.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using indefinite pronouns as the object of a verb or preposition.

positives: I didn't know anyone at the party.
He saw nothing there.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns ('something', 'nobody') as subjects, with a singular verb.
example_raw:
I was so confused that I thought something was happening. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Unfortunately something has happened with the airplane's schedule, so I won't be able to arrive at 1.15 pm, as we agreed. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

So I tried to call for help, but nobody answered. (Czech Republic; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Czech; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Indefinite entities initiating action or possessing a state.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using indefinite pronouns as subjects taking singular verbs.

positives: Something is happening.
Nobody was there.

can_do_statement: Can use indefinite pronouns with a relative clause to form complex noun phrases, to give focus.
example_raw:
Something that I like very much is the idea of the classes. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Greek; Pass)

Something extra, which is not really pleasant, is their behavior. (B2 VANTAGE; 2006; Polish; Pass)

Something really good about it is that it'd give us some work experience, which we don't have right now. (Uruguay; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Everything that I believed changed and without any help I managed to write perfectly, according to my teacher. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Greek; Pass)

Everyone who can use a computer can use the new products. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Chinese; Fail)

ontology.mental_model: Focusing on a specific aspect of an indefinite entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Modifying indefinite pronouns with a relative clause.

positives: Something that I really like is the food.
Everyone who can help should come.

can_do_statement: Can use 'anything' in an ellipted clause, ('if there is anything …').
example_raw:
Anything else you need, ask Sarah. (Portugal; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

Anything you need in connection with my report, please don't hesitate to contact me. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1999; Spanish - European; Pass)

Anything you want to ask me, feel free to do so. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Open condition or request without explicit condition.

positives: Anything you need, just ask.
Anything else you want, let me know.
negatives: If there is anything you need, ask me.

can_do_statement: Can use premodifiers with indefinite pronouns, often to intensify.
example_raw:
You can find absolutely anything, whatever you need. (Kazakhstan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Kazakh; Pass)

I like to wear a T-shirt with jeans almost everywhere I go. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)

Nearly everyone I know sits at a computer all day. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using words like 'absolutely' or 'almost' before indefinite pronouns.

positives: I can find absolutely anything in this store.
Nearly everyone agrees with me.
negatives: I can find anything in this store.

can_do_statement: Can use 'anything' with post-modifiers to form complex noun phrases as subjects with a singular verb, to give focus.
example_raw:
Anything else can be attached too if needed. (China; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Chinese; Pass)

Anything to show how happy you are for them will do. (Korea, South; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Korean; Pass)

Anything that puts you in contact with the English language is important. (C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Focusing on any entity that meets specific conditions.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'anything' modified by a phrase or clause as the subject.

positives: Anything that makes you happy is fine.
Anything to eat will do.
negatives: I don't have anything that makes you happy.

can_do_statement: Can use the full range of indefinite pronouns as subjects, with a singular verb.
example_raw:
But, nowadays nothing is free, so you have to pay for everything. (Hungary; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Hungarian; Pass)

Her parents had told her everything weeks ago; she had cried and argued, but nothing could change her parents’ opinion. (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; German; Pass)

Yes it was Christmas, that's why everybody tried to smile. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

Everywhere is green and clean. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 2003; Turkish; Pass)

When we came back home, everywhere was very untidy. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Fail)

I searched my car to see if anything was missing. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Full range of indefinite entities initiating action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using indefinite pronouns as subjects with a singular verb.

positives: Everything is fine now.
Everybody tried to smile.

can_do_statement: Can use indefinite pronouns in vague expressions to refer to things in a non-specific way.
example_raw:
Is it worth having a nervous breakdown or anything like that? (Portuguese, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993 )

My personal idea to help the environment is to try to plant more trees around the college, for example, in the zone behind the college or somewhere else. (B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Other; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using phrases like 'or something', 'or anything like that'.

positives: We could go to the park or something.
I didn't have a cold or anything like that.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'of' in the phrases 'a friend of mine' and 'friends of mine'.
example_raw:
A friend of mine gave me a present for my birthday. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

Some friends of mine were here with me too. (Key English Test; A2; Portuguese)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'of mine' instead of 'my' for emphasis or variation.

positives: A friend of mine gave me this book.
I saw some friends of mine yesterday.
negatives: My friend gave me this book.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours', with singular reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
example_raw:
It was my best present, although I also loved yours. (Key English Test; A2; Spanish-European)

My favourite meal is spaghetti with garlic bread. What's yours? (Key English Test for Schools; A2; Tagalog)

To go to my house from yours, take the first on the right, Victoria Road, and there is an underground station. (Key English Test; A2; French)

I bought a pink mobile. It's like yours. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Turkish; Pass)

So that's all about my mobile phone. Please write to me about yours too! (Key English Test; A2;Turkish)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'yours' instead of 'your + noun' as an object or complement.

positives: I also loved yours.
It's like yours.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine', with singular and plural reference, in subject and object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
example_raw:
I bought a new jacket because mine was very old. (Key English Test; A2; Italian)

I bought a pullover and trousers because mine are too small for me. (Key English Test; A2; Korean)

The phone is not mine. (Key English Test; A2 Czech) 

You should bring your computer games and Maths book. I have lost mine. (Key English Test; A2; Turkish) 

I want to give you a birthday present like mine. (Key English Test; A2; Chinese)

ontology.mental_model: First-person singular possession as an independent entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'mine' as a standalone pronoun in various positions.

positives: The phone is not mine.
Mine are too small for me.
negatives: He works in a coal mine.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours' after noun + 'of'.
example_raw:
Maybe you can take a friend of yours with you there. (Preliminary English Test; B1; German)

I think that it's a very good idea of yours to come to the UK. (Skills for Life (Entry 3); Spanish)

You can ask some friends of yours to join you. (Preliminary English Test; B1; Greek)

ontology.mental_model: Second-person possession expressed via prepositional phrase.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'of yours' after a noun for emphasis or variation.

positives: You can take a friend of yours.
It was a good idea of yours.
